messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Data Table Cell hyperlinks ?
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Data Table Cell hyperlinks ?
messages.body_plain:
Yes, I think it is possible. If you are familiar with .on() in jQuery
(http://api.jquery.com/on/), you can add such click events on <td>
cells. It is just a little awkward to give you an example at the
moment, since we are transitioning from DataTables 1.9.x to 1.10.2
(https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/558), which has a new API. Once
the new version is in shiny, what you need to do is to provide a
callback function in renderDataTable(), e.g.

renderDataTable(..., callback = "
function(table) {
  table.on('click.dt', 'td', function(event) {
    // ....
})
}
")

Of course, it is not impossible to work with the old version of
DataTables if you read the old documentation at
http://legacy.datatables.net.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject_clean: Error deploying shiny app: could not find function "rep_len"
messages.body_plain:
Nick, (and Nate)

The error is coming from shinyapps package, not from your code. There are references to "rep_len" within shinyapps, and therefore (at the moment) it won't work with R versions of lower than 3.0.0. Would it be possible for you to upgrade your version of R? We are evaluating what the minimum supported version of R should be, and it is good to hear from you and others if there is any strong reason to stay with R 2.15.x.

Best,
Fereshteh

messages.body_plain:
Hi Fereshteh,

All of my local instances of R are upgraded to version 3+; where I'm stuck is developing my shiny app on RStudio's Spark server which seems still to be running R 2.15.3. Here is a related thread, where several other RStudio staff are responding to a user's question about server updates: https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/shiny-discuss/Ve9YBbl99iQ.

Any additional thoughts on how to work with the shinyapps package on that server, or suggestions on where else to try developing the code?

Nick

> cells. It is just a little awkward to give you an example at the
> moment, since we are transitioning from DataTables 1.9.x to 1.10.2
> (https://github.com/rstudio/shiny/pull/558), which has a new API. Once
> the new version is in shiny, what you need to do is to provide a
> callback function in renderDataTable(), e.g.
>
> renderDataTable(..., callback = "

>   table.on('click.dt', 'td', function(event) {
>     // ....
> })
> }
> ")
>
> Of course, it is not impossible to work with the old version of
> DataTables if you read the old documentation at
> http://legacy.datatables.net.
>

messages.subject: RQuantLib package on shinyapps?
messages.subject_clean: RQuantLib package on shinyapps?
messages.body_plain:
Hi all,

I was trying to use RQuantLib package on shinyapps that was working fine on my windows machine with R. After running deployApp() I get the following error.

configure: error: Please install QuantLib before trying to build RQuantLib.
ERROR: configuration failed for package â€˜RQuantLibâ€™
* removing â€˜/usr/local/lib/R/site-library/RQuantLibâ€™
################################### End Log ###################################
Error: Unhandled Exception: Child Task 819470 failed: Error building image: Error building RQuantLib (0.3.12). Build exited with non-zero status: 1

basically it says QuantLib is not installed on the machine (I guess the shinyapps server?). Problem is QuantLib is not a CRAN package, and from the search results I got online (http://r.789695.n4.nabble.com/RQuantLib-Quantlib-for-R-3-0-2-Linux-td4679609.html), for Linux machines (I guess what the shinyapps server runs) you need to install that QuantLib package manually. Is there a way that I can do it on my end, or I have to contact the shinyapps admin to do it?

Thanks!

messages.body_plain:
Hey all,

I have written and deployed an app located here: http://ctloftin.shinyapps.io/fantasy/

Basically it reads in data from a csv file and outputs it in a table. When a player is selected from the drop-down list and then the "Drafted" button is clicked, that player is removed from the list of available players in the data frame. When the page is reloaded, the data should be re-read from the csv file. However, when I do reload the page, the data is never read in again. I can access the app on one computer, draft a player, and then load on another computer, where then the player is still not included even though it's a brand-new run of the app. The only way I can get the data in it's original form is to completely terminate the app from the server and redeploy which obviously defeats the whole purpose.

This is my relevant code:

draftdata <- read.csv(file="fpprojections.csv")
shinyServer(function(input, output, clientData, session) {
}

As you can see, the data should be read in only once per visit since it is outside the shinyServer function. I have tried terminating the app from the server and redeploying to no avail. Any thoughts/suggestions would be much appreciated.

Thanks,
Colin

messages.body_plain:
Hi Colin,

It might help to read this part of Shiny tutorial:
http://shiny.rstudio.com/tutorial/lesson5/

especially the section on "Execution". This is from that section:

"Source scripts, load libraries, and read data sets at the beginning of server.R outside of theshinyServer function. Shiny will only run this code once, which is all you need to set your server up to run the R expressions contained in shinyServer."

According to this, your data is only read once when application is loaded and R process has started. This R process on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> is able to serve 20 different connections. When you launch your page on a different browser or machine, it won't start a new R process; it will still re-use the same R process. Which means it will not re-read the data file. Does this make sense?

Best,
Fereshteh

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] problem with hosting shiny application
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] problem with hosting shiny application
messages.body_plain:
Hi Siva,
You should be able to run more than one app per user on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> since we actually start up three R processes per application.  That being said, we haven't exposed the fine tuning parameters that would allow you to restrict a single user to a single R process, nor have we surfaced the capability to start up an arbitrary number of R processes.  Today, your best bet on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> would be to create N number of apps with different names:  DNAapp01, DNAapp02, DNAapp03,etc....

As for deploying on your own Shiny server install, I would recommend using the support.rstudio.com <http://support.rstudio.com> forum seek help regarding configuration and operation of Shiny Server.

Best,
Tareef

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Referring to data files from more than 1 app
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Referring to data files from more than 1 app
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andy,

You can't share data across apps by including them in any one of the apps.  You would want to put them in a shared storage location like an S3, a database, or have them download the data from a common location.

Here is the relevant paragraphs from the getting started guide <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/shinyapps.html>:

1) Data written by an application to the local filesystem of an instance will be lost when you re-deploy the app. Additionally, the distributed nature of the ShinyApps.io platform means that instances may be shut down and re-created at any time for maintenance or to recover from server failures.

2) It is possible to have more than one instance of an application. This situation means that multiple instances of an application do not share a local filesystem. A file written to one instance will not be available to another instance.

We are considering whether we need to provide a shared data store of some kind, but we haven't gotten enough data to help us determine whether those added features would be ones that would be useful premium features.

-Tareef

messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Path problems referring to an app
messages.body_plain:
Hi Andy,
Shinyapps is designed to be a distributed platform for the deployment of shiny applications.  Each application is completely self contained and runs within it's own "mini virtual machine".  The best way to think about may well be to think of every deployment of every app running on its own computer.  We manage the setting up, configuration, running, and shutdown of those computers on your behalf.

There is no shared filesystem that you can leverage today, but it might be a feature we would consider building in the future should the demand justify it.
Best,
-Tareef

messages.body_plain:
Hi Andy,
We don't have storage limits yet.  The limit is really on the upload of the files you can send out on a per app basis.  The limit is currently set to 100MB.  Do you think that will work for you?
We would love to learn more about the use cases to understand what else we need to be supporting in shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> for it to be a platform that works for you.

Best,
Tareef

messages.body_plain:
Tareef
  I am currently mainly doing toy examples. One I am developing has a significant storage is a csv file in the 10s of megs - but I can presumably reduce this either via compression
or as an rds.
 I currently have a sports stats website based on Flash with an MS SQL backend.but was hoping to switch to a shiny site with probably a SQLite db., probaby doable as one app (albeit complicated). However, I would want to do a lot of ad hoc analyses based on the same db, which I had hoped to be able to incorporate in a kind of rMarkdown blog. messages.subject: [8/12/14] New Shinyapps package and enhancements to shinyapps.io
messages.subject_clean: [8/12/14] New Shinyapps package and enhancements to shinyapps.io
messages.body_plain:
Dear shinyapps users,

Over the past few weeks we have been working hard on quite a few changes, and we thought it was time to announce them to you all and gather some feedback.  For those just starting out, or if you signed up for Shinyapps but haven’t gotten started because you were intimidated by our instructions, check out this article <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/shinyapps.html>.

For existing users, our investments have been primarily focused on making the platform more robust, faster, and easier for you to see and correct errors that may be occurring in your application.

Reliability -- changes introduced over the past 3 weeks have improved the reliability of the service and resulted in a five fold decrease in the errors reported.

Performance -- speed improvements for application start times have been measured at 3 to 5 times faster since the changes rolled out.

Visibility/debugging - a new version of the shinyapps package has been released which you can use to explore the logs of your running application (check out shinyapps::showLogs()  in this article <http://shiny.rstudio.com/articles/shinyapps.html>).  Please note that you will need to install the latest version of the shinyapps package from github and to redeploy your application.

Thank you all for your help in improving the shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> platform.  Over the coming weeks we will be making additional improvements to the build and deploy times for applications, and adding support for additional R packages.  We look forward to your feedback as always.

Best,

The Shinyapps team

PS.  As of this morning we have added support for the nloptr <http://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/nloptr/index.html> package.

However even if the calculation is fast, the page is not responding to a second access until the first access got the results.

I read that this is a feature of ShinyServer Pro.
Is it possible to change the number of instances for an application? So that basically two independent accesses to the webpage could be handled simultaneously?

If I try to change the number of instances:
shinyapps::configureApp("riskcalc", size = "small", instances = 2)
Error: /v1/applications/17201/properties/application.instances.count 400 - Unable to set read-only property.

Do you have any advice on the problem? Or is this feature just not available in this alpha testing.

thanks,
josef

messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] configureApp() number of instances
messages.body_plain:
Hi Josef,
You are correct in your understanding that the second request is waiting for the first because it is going to the same R process. The single container we start today does allow for up to 3 R processes to start but I believe the additional processes don't get added until the prior R process has 18 connections.   That being said adding additional instances is something we are working on right now, and we will share the command that you would need to use to enable it hopefully in the coming few weeks.
We also suspect that we will need to surface the ability to tune the algorithm for how many connections you want per R process and possibly even the number of R processes per container.

All of these features are on the docket for the beta of the service.
Tareef

So it looks like i figured it out. I was saving my workspaces (.Rdata files) in the same directory which the deploy runs on. Since these files had grown quite large it looks like it started interfering with the deployment process. Eventhough when these .Rdata files were much smaller in previous versions of my app, it did not affect the deployment process. My workaround was simply to move all these .Rdata files somewhere else and re-run deployApp(). messages.body_plain:
Hi Andrew,
When building an app for Shinyapps, you have a few choices:

1. Bundle the data with the app (all files you would use would need to be in the directory of the ui.R and server.R or in a sub-directory.
2. Access the data from the internet/web in some way.  That could include a database that can be accessed remotely, an S3 bucket that you can read from, or a web service.

The paradigm is a bit confusing at first, and we are certainly open to finding ways of simplifying it so that it is a bit easier to grok.

Hope this helps.
-Tareef

messages.body_plain:
Hello,
 I have a app. up on ShinyApps and all is working well. I have noticed one issue that surprised me. I have a list of plant names, some of which start with capital letters ("Norway maple") some of which start with lower case letters ("red maple"). I have done all of my coding using a windows desktop. I am using these names as choices in a selectInput. To put them  in the correct order I am using a variation on

selectInput( inputId='myId", label="whatever", choices=c(Names[ order(Names) ] )

messages.subject: Re: ShinyApps.io and Iframes
messages.subject_clean: ShinyApps.io and Iframes
messages.body_plain:
To add,

It appears if your Shinyapp requires a login - this can't be done through the iframe.
An incorrect user/password is recognized and alerted to.
But a correct one just reloads the same login screen without passing you through to the app.

If you log in to the app in a separate browser window, and then access it through the iframe everything works fine.

/Vasilios

> It does actually load plain.
>
> I was trying to POST the login credentials through it, but without success.
> Is there a reason why this should not work do you think?
> Alternatively, is there a way to pre-populate the login form - allowing the user to send the form?
>
> There are good reasons for this setup in our environment, but I can understand if this is not possible due to security issues.
>
> Thanks again,
> Vasilios
>

messages.body_plain:

 "application unexpectedly exited.

messages.body_plain:
Hello everyone,

I just discovered ShinyApps and find it really nice.
Unfortunately, I have a problem with the user I created...

I registered into the ShinyApps website using my GitHub account, created a ShinyApps user and deployed a simple Shiny application. Everything worked perfectly fine.
Then, I had to change my GitHub primary email address in my Github profile, and I made it private.
My problem is that now, when I log in ShinyApps.io, the website recognizes me but somehow lost track of my previously created user. I can't create it again (it still exists). And I can't see my running app in the dashboard while it is still running: I can access it directly through its URL.

I tried to revert to my previous email address in GitHub, and log back into ShinyApps website with no effect. For an unknown reason, the email address in ShinyApps.io is not updated any more.

Do you have any idea what I could do to recover access to my user?

Thanks in advance!

Céline

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] I authorized my computer through shinyapps::setAccountInfo, but I still can't use shinyapps.io
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] I authorized my computer through shinyapps::setAccountInfo, but I still can't use shinyapps.io
messages.body_plain:
The authorization that you are copying form shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> is for your R process to talk to shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> (so you can deploy your application).  Whereas the login screen you see for shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> when you visit it with a browser is for authenticating you (the publisher) to see your account information.

Sorry about the confusion.

-Tareef

It can be a firewall issue. Downloading the zip package from Github
might have failed during devtools::install_github(). See if you are
able to download
https://github.com/rstudio/shinyapps/archive/master.zip If you can,
unzip it, and use

  R CMD INSTALL shinyapps-master

to install it in a command window. Well, I do not know how much you
know about R CMD INSTALL...

Do not use utils:::menuInstallPkgs(). The zip package you downloaded
is not really a Windows binary package for R; it is just a normal zip
archive of the source package.

Regards,
Yihui

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] how does shinyApps.io works.
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] how does shinyApps.io works.
messages.body_plain:
Siva,

I am not sure I understand your question, but I will do my best to explain what happens when a application is deployed to ShinyApps in terms of where packages come from.

Calling deployApp() examines the source files in your application and creates a list of package dependencies with the package description for each package. This list and the source files get uploaded to the ShinyApps servers as a tarball. Once uploaded, the dependency list is examined and the providence of each package is determined from the package description. If the package source is supported (CRAN, GitHub, etc), the source files for the package are downloaded and the package is compiled. Once compiled, the package get installed onto a "virtual machine", along with the source files and the application is started. One thing to note is that if a package has already compiled, a cached copy of the binary is installed rather then rebuilding from source.

Hope that helps, let me know if you have further questions.

-Andy

messages.subject: Re: [shinyapps-users] Does ShinyApps have some problem with date formats/dates?
messages.subject_clean: [shinyapps-users] Does ShinyApps have some problem with date formats/dates?
messages.body_plain:
The issue is that apps running on ShinyApps do not have any locale set (or more precisely apps on ShinyApps use a generic non-country/language specific locale, that does not have LC_TIME set). This breaks using some strfime() parameters including %b.

As work around, you can use %m for the numeric representation of the month.

This is an issue we hope to correct in the future, by detecting locale information from the client, and using the same locale on the server.

-Andy

messages.body_plain:
Justin,

Glad to hear it's working. I think the issue was that the package author changed his username from karthikram to karthik since you installed the package from GitHub. The GitHub username is recorded when you install a package from GitHub using devtools. If it changes, ShinyApps will be unable to find the package source. A somewhat unlikely scenario, but possible.

-Andy

Fereshteh

messages.body_plain:
Oops, my sincere apologies for not sharing the code (and also for the short absence from this group because of which I couldn't respond to you timely.

I tried to identify the error on my own, hoping to prevent taking a lot of your time on this one. I think your guess was correct: the error is due to the stemDocument function in the tm package. When I use the function, no character vectors are returned at all. When I do not use it, everything is fine. I checked the SnowballC package, which seems to be the place from which tm package uses the stemmer.
It says: Elements of the vector are converted to UTF-8 encoding before the stemming is performed, and the returned elements are marked as such when they contain non-ASCII characters.
When I run the same function locally, however, things are fine. It is just a problem when I use runApp() or if I have deployed the application already.

Would you like to make any observations about this?
Link to the app is: https://kazmialiarsalan.shinyapps.io/sampleApp/
Link to the code is: https://github.com/noobuseR/testApp

I am currently checking if the original problem (with the original app) is also similar.

Many thanks for your time.

My app: https://amit.shinyapps.io/WordCloudMaker/
My github: https://github.com/mexindian/Wordcloud.from.folder

Just to say I was also having a problem with my app working correctly locally but on shinyapps.io <http://shinyapps.io> I would get the error:

no applicable method for 'meta' applied to an object of class "try-error"

After reading this discussion I removed the following from my server.R
if(input$stem) c <- tm_map(c, stemDocument)

and also on my ui.R where that could be selected. I was suspicious because this isn't called unless the checkbox is checked, and there was a problem as soon as I selected the file to upload... And indeed, this step was not sufficient, I still had the same error.

The problem went away when I removed these two lines:

c <- tm_map(c, stripWhitespace)
c <- tm_map(c, removeNumbers)

Which were the two functions that were running immediately. So I think that rather than the problem being with the *stemming* function, the problem is with tm_map.

Amit Kohli,

Thanks for sharing your solution. However, I think that tm_map itself may not be the problem, because in my app, the removeNumbers is not being used with the tm_map function, neither is the word stemming function. I do acknowledge that for stripping white spaces I used the tm_map function. This did not present any problem, still. And problem only occurs when I try to stem my words.

Link to the app is: https://kazmialiarsalan.shinyapps.io/sampleApp/ <https://www.google.com/url?q=https%3A%2F%2Fkazmialiarsalan.shinyapps.io%2FsampleApp%2F&sa=D&sntz=1&usg=AFQjCNFBkpOqDpC0ToxbhOzP4a1Evy4lzg>

Yihui,

In addition to the problem described above in a sample app (that stemming removes all character data - presumably this may be an encoding issue. But I do not know how to resolve this...), I have managed to create another short version of the app that produces the same error as faced originally:

This is the link to this new app: https://kazmialiarsalan.shinyapps.io/test/
This is the link to my code: https://github.com/noobuseR/testAppNew

We may focus on this original problem - I shared the other problem because 1. I think the two problems are related, and 2. I am hoping that it may give you some insight into the source of this error.

HTH

> The problem went away when I removed these two lines:
>
> c <- tm_map(c, stripWhitespace)
> c <- tm_map(c, removeNumbers)
>
> Which were the two functions that were running immediately. So I think that rather than the problem being with the *stemming* function, the problem is with tm_map.
>
>
>

When I do not use it, everything is fine. I checked the SnowballC package, which seems to be the place from which tm package uses the stemmer.
> > > It says: Elements of the vector are converted to UTF-8 encoding before the stemming is performed, and the returned elements are marked as such when they contain non-ASCII characters.

> > > > reproducible example.
> > > >
> > > > Regards,
> > > > Yihui
